title: Implement VaultProjection: render KnowledgeObject → Obsidian Markdown note
description:
First concrete implementation of the Projection trait. Rust — alcanzai-core.

Reference: v0.1.x markdown_writer.py and note-template design (salvage protocol: read for behavioral reference, reimplement fresh against Projection trait). See prototype/markdown_writer.py.

VaultProjection struct:
  Config: VaultConfig { vault_root: PathBuf, note_subdir: Option<PathBuf> }.
  render(library, config): incremental — for each KnowledgeObject where updated_at > last_render_watermark, write/overwrite its note file.
  rebuild(library, config): delete vault_root/note_subdir, then render all objects.

Note file layout (per v0.1.x reference):
  Filename: <KnowledgeObjectId>.md (stable, UUID-based — survives metadata corrections).
  YAML frontmatter: title, authors (list), year, content_type, doi (if present), arxiv_id (if present), alcanzai_id (KnowledgeObjectId), source_plugin, fetched_at.
  Sections: ## Abstract (if present), ## Content (blocks rendered as flowing text), ## Enrichments (per enricher, JSON or structured list).
  Wikilinks: [[<KnowledgeObjectId>|title]] format for cross-references (used later by citation graph projection).

Constraints:
  - rebuild() must make ZERO LLM calls (renders existing Library state only).
  - render/rebuild must be deterministic: same Library state → same file content.
  - Both operations write only to vault_root; never modify the Library.

Unit tests:
  - Single KnowledgeObject → expected Markdown output (snapshot test).
  - rebuild on empty library → empty vault dir (no files).
  - rebuild idempotency: two rebuilds produce identical files.

Acceptance criterion: tests pass; cargo fmt + clippy clean; rebuild makes no external calls.
